# Scarlet Macaw, Green-winged Scarlet Macaw

​​Red-and-green Macaw. Ara chloropterus​​​​.

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [University Park](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque)
- [Biotic Inventory](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico)
- Scarlet Macaw, Green-winged Scarlet Macaw

[![Image of a scarlet macaw, green-winged scarlet macaw](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/3a5116a2-6286-487b-9cef-eb0b2ce9eb39/web/guacamaya-roja.jpg)](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico/guacamaya-roja)

![](https://www.eafit.edu.co/universidad-parque/inventario-biotico/guacamaya-roja)

###### Etymology

Ara corresponds to an indigenous Brazilian name in the Tupi language. Chloropterus derives from the Greek word cholos, meaning green, and pteron, meaning wing: it alludes to the distinctive greenish coloration of the wing coverts, which differentiates it from Ara macao.

###### Description

Large in size (84-96 cm), with a deep scarlet plumage, similar to that of the Scarlet Macaw (Ara macao), from which it differs in its darker red and wing coloration. Its bare face is ivory with thin lines of red feathers. The iris is ivory. The bill is whitish above and blackish below. The wings have sky-blue tips, and the midwings are green, extending to the back and becoming very conspicuous both at rest and in flight when viewed from above. The rump and tail tip are blue. Underside, the wings and tail are dark red. The legs are black.

###### Ecology

It inhabits lowland, humid and semi-humid forests, gallery forests on plains and foothills, savannas with scattered trees, and partially open areas. It is found in primary forests of the plains and low hills. Like most macaws, they nest in tree cavities, rocky outcrops, and other steep areas, occasionally in ravine hollows. Clutches consist of one to four white eggs, although three is most common. They consume a wide variety of fruits from trees and palms, especially those of the genera Endopleura, Hymenaea, and Bertholletia. They also eat leaves, flower buds, flowers, and seeds, among other things.

###### Distribution

It can be found from southeastern Panama to northern Argentina, Paraguay, and southern Brazil. In Colombia, it inhabits areas between 0 and 500 meters above sea level, but can reach elevations of up to 1000 meters. Its distribution is discontinuous; it is found in the Serranía de Perijá, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the San Jorge River valley, the upper valleys of the Sinú, Ranchería, and Cesar rivers, the Pacific coast as far south as the Serranía del Baudó, western Antioquia, and east of the Andes in Norte de Santander, the Eastern Plains, the Catatumbo region, the Orinoquia, and the Amazon. In the Aburrá Valley, some individuals that have been released or have escaped from captivity can be observed. At EAFIT University, they have been seen sporadically moving around the campus, but they do not remain there continuously.
